summary: Intermittent control-plane auth failures and gRPC keepalive resets from private deployment behind VXLAN overlay (MTU mismatch)
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent control-plane authentication failures and frequent gRPC keepalive resets for their Private deployment. The failures began after a network vendor upgrade that introduced an overlay VXLAN fabric between on-prem aggregation routers and the VPC transit gateway.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a multi-shard model request via customer's Private deployment (region us-west-2) to trigger control-plane token refresh and model artifact streaming.
2) Observe gRPC keepalive probes between serving nodes and control-plane endpoints when under sustained 90-110 rps request load.
3) Correlate with times when upstream overlay path is used (VXLAN encapsulation) vs fallback underlay path.
4) Reproduce by toggling the overlay interface MTU on a test path (1500 -> 1400) while streaming a ~20MB model shard range request.

Expected: Stable gRPC sessions and successful token refresh/manifest fetches without transient auth errors. Observed: Periodic gRPC stream resets, token refresh failures (401), and partial shard reads (retries).
logs: control-plane/auth: 401 token refresh error for instance i-0abcd1234 (error=stream-reset)
tcpdump: [fragmented] outer-ethertype=0x0800 vxlan vni 100 inner IP len 1600 -> indicates inner frame larger than underlay MTU
artifact-fetch: range-request partial, server returned 206 but subsequent GET returned truncated chunk, client logged EPIPE
customers-net-device: syslog: vxlan: packet-too-large, dropped frame
comments: 2026-03-01 09:17 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer opened with symptoms: intermittent 401s during token refresh, spikes of gRPC keepalive resets. Noticed outage windows map to vendor upgrade time window.
2026-03-01 11:02 - Carlos Alvarez (SRE): Asked customer for pcap and traceroute from a serving node to control-plane endpoints; requested MTU and overlay config from their network team.

2026-03-01 15:28 - Customer (NetOps - Jamie Lin): Uploaded pcaps and confirmed VXLAN VNI=100 with underlay MTU 1400 after upgrade; previously underlay was 1500. Noted some devices report 'fragmentation required' errors.

2026-03-02 08:45 - Carlos Alvarez (SRE): We observed repeated inner packet lengths > 1500 inside VXLAN encapsulation leading to underlay fragmentation or drops. Hypothesis: overlay encapsulation expands inner frames past the underlay MTU causing fragments to be dropped or reordered, which impacts gRPC keepalive timing and TLS record boundaries, resulting in token refresh failures.

2026-03-02 12:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Added mitigation steps for customer to try (lower MSS/MTU on endpoints, enable DF path MTU discovery fallback) and asked for confirmation on whether TSO/GSO were enabled on their hosts.

2026-03-03 09:33 - Customer (Jamie Lin): Applied temporary MTU increase on underlay nodes (to 9000) and disabled TX offload on serving hosts; reported gRPC resets reduced to near-zero for a 4-hour test window.

2026-03-04 14:21 - Carlos Alvarez (SRE): Verified with packet captures that when underlay MTU matched the encapsulated frame size, no inner fragmentation was present and TLS records remained contiguous. Planning final resolution steps and proposed a permanent network configuration change.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: VXLAN encapsulation increased packet size beyond underlay MTU; fragments get dropped or reordered by intermediate devices, breaking gRPC/TLS expectations.

Hypothesis 2: Host-side TCP segmentation offload (TSO/GSO) combined with small underlay MTU leads to large offloaded segments that are fragmented by network, causing corrupted TLS record boundaries on the receiver.
Test performed: Ran tcpdump on serving-node and underlay router. Observed outer (encapsulating) packets with length > 1500 and intermediate syslog messages 'packet-too-large' on vendor gear.
Test performed: Disabled TSO/GSO on serving nodes (ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off) and re-ran streaming tests; saw immediate reduction in keepalive resets.
Correlation: Incident windows aligned with vendor overlay rollforward which changed default underlay MTU from 1500 to 1400 and enabled VXLAN with 50 bytes overhead.
Related notes: Customer's PMTU discovery was intermittently blocked by an inline firewall which returned ICMP unreachable inconsistently, worsening the fragmentation behavior.
Observed side-effects: Partial artifact reads and retries added latency, provoking more frequent token refresh attempts that then hit race conditions during short-lived stream resets.
resolution: Short-term workaround (applied by customer): Increased underlay MTU to jumbo frames (9000) on aggregation routers and disabled TSO/GSO on serving hosts. Result: gRPC resets and token refresh 401 frequency dropped to near zero in validation window.

Root cause: VXLAN overlay encapsulation created inner packets that exceeded underlay MTU; intermediate gear dropped or mishandled fragments and ICMP PMTU messages were intermittently blocked by an inline firewall, breaking TLS/gRPC assumptions and causing token refresh races.
- Preferred: Align underlay MTU to account for VXLAN overhead (increase MTU or enable jumbo frames across fabric) and ensure PMTU ICMPs are permitted end-to-end.

- Alternative: Configure host-level MSS clamping to reduce inner packet sizes (e.g., iptables/netfilter rule to clamp MSS to 1350) and keep TSO/GSO disabled on serving hosts if hardware offload is incompatible.
- Add monitoring: SRE recommends adding synthetic long-range artifact fetch checks and a packet-fragmentation gauge to the customer's network dashboards to detect regressions.

Action items completed: Customer implemented underlay MTU change and host TSO/GSO disable; SRE provided a short runbook for MSS clamping and PMTU verification. Follow-up scheduled to verify stability over 7 days.
Follow-up: Recommend change request with network vendor to ensure VXLAN MTU requirements documented and for firewall rule to allow ICMP 'Fragmentation needed' messages to flow.
